notes:
# The free trial actually counts now {sparkle}
It has been appearance only: a chip in the toolbar over a recorder that
recorded whatever it was asked to. Runs are counted against this Mac now,
reported exactly once, and a run the server never heard about is queued and
re-reported rather than lost — one trial had been split across two machine
ids because ioreg timed out mid-recording, so the id is read once and kept.

# A spent trial says so before the meeting, not after it {clock}
The refusal arrives at the scheduler, at Record now, and at the offer that
appears over a live meeting, each saying so rather than quietly doing
nothing. A meeting armed beyond what the trial covers is flagged the moment
it is armed — in the list, on the schedule, and after the last recording
that fits — because finding out afterwards means the meeting is gone.

# Trial recordings are watermarked, and say so first {video}
720p at 15fps with a tiled mark, written into the file as it is made rather
than painted on afterwards. The quality cards say which of them a trial can
reach before one is chosen, so the limit is met on the settings page instead
of in a finished recording of something that cannot be recorded again.

# The meeting can be told it is being recorded {notes}
Switch it on and one line goes into Zoom's own chat when recording starts,
so the people in the meeting are told without anybody having to remember.
It is put into the chat box through Accessibility rather than typed, because
typed characters land wherever the focus happens to be and in Zoom's meeting
window the letters are shortcuts — mute, video, screen share — while Return
presses whatever button has focus. Off unless it is turned on, and the app
asks once, the first time a meeting is armed without it, whether everybody
knows.

# Notes can be turned on halfway through a recording {sparkle}
Deciding you want a summary is something that happens during a meeting
rather than before it, and the switch was locked for the whole run. It stays
live now, along with the question to ask, and what is set is what gets read
when the capture ends — the link, the time and the repeat stay locked,
because those describe a run that is happening.

# Buying it is one page {shield_lock}
The price sits beside what it buys, the rules are three lines rather than a
document, and the thank-you screen carries the marks of what has just been
unlocked — including on a page that is already open, so activating from the
Upgrade panel no longer leaves somebody looking at the lock they have just
paid to remove.

# The welcome screen is one page {info}
It was three: the welcome, the System Check, then a first meeting to point
it at. The check step re-ran every permission test while building itself —
proving Screen Recording means capturing a frame — so it blocked the window
for seconds to re-derive an answer that had just landed, and the System
Check opens by itself anyway when something needs granting. It explains what
the trial counts, which nobody running an earlier build has been shown, so
it appears once more after this update and never on a licensed Mac.

# Opening the app is about two seconds quicker {stepper}
The window asked the Keychain whether this Mac is licensed twenty-one times
while building itself — the toolbar, the trial chip, the licence page and
the form each asking independently, none knowing the others just had — and
each ask shells out to security at about 27ms, which was over half of the
launch, all on the thread that answers clicks. The answer is held for five
seconds now: long enough to collapse a burst like that into one read, short
enough that a key activated elsewhere is noticed almost at once.

# Two runs of one meeting make one file {film}
A meeting interrupted — the Mac slept, the app was replaced — becomes a
second recording beside the first, and nothing offered to join them. They
merge oldest first now, and the parts can go to the Trash once the result
has been measured: ffmpeg can abandon a join halfway and still leave
something playable, so a merged file that plays for less than its parts did
deletes nothing and says why.

---

Everything else in this release:

- The read view says what is happening while it is happening, rather than
  "Recorded successfully" over last week's file.
- The microphone setting follows the choice that turns it on, notices access
  granted in System Settings without a relaunch, and asks before a meeting
  is saved with somebody's own voice in it.
- Every toast raised on Settings or Invitations was drawn behind the page:
  saving settings, the alert test, the copied licence key, all of them.
- Closing the window during a recording lost the app.
- install.sh refuses to replace the app while a recording is running — the
  window and the recorder are the same binary, and quitting one to install
  once cost a meeting nine minutes in.
- Spoken announcements are behind one flag rather than removed.
- The consent question is its own panel: what would be posted, readable
  before it is agreed to, and two answers that are both something to do.
- checks/sandbox.py answers that question, so no test harness stops on a
  modal nobody is there to press.
